subject: Post-call: Long-context evals and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: Long-context evals and next steps

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a shared plan.

Recap:
- Goal: evaluate model fit for Acme's long-context use case (one-off documents up to ~50k tokens; ideal behavior: high-fidelity summarization, low truncation loss).
- Key concerns you raised: truncation behavior, summarization fidelity across >32k contexts, latency/cost tradeoffs, and data residency.

Redwood recommendations (initial):
- Candidate models to evaluate: Redwood-13B-32k (quantized) for balanced cost/quality, Redwood-RT-30B for highest fidelity on long summaries, and Redwood-7B-8k as a low-cost baseline with retrieval/chunking.
- Approach: run an automated long-context eval using your prompt set + a few 50k token samples. We'll measure: truncation rate, ROUGE/ROUGE-L/bert-score vs. your reference summaries, and prompt-trimming failure modes.

Deliverables we propose:
1) Run a 48–72 hour eval: we take your redacted samples + the attached prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) and produce a results CSV (acme_eval_results_20260720.csv) with per-sample metrics and example outputs.
2) Short write-up highlighting failure modes and recommended serving pattern (single-window model if <=32k; chunk+RAG+stitching for >32k; suggested quantization/profile).
3) Optional POC: 2-week PoC on Redwood Dedicated to validate end-to-end latency and cost at scale.

Next steps (please):
- Can you share 2–3 redacted sample documents (50k token examples) and a reference summary for a subset? If needed we can accept a Drive link or S3.
- Confirm data residency needs (do samples need to stay in EU/US-only infra?).
- I'll schedule Ben for a deep-dive on chunking/serving patterns if you want technical detail.

I've attached the prompt set we discussed and a simple eval template. Ben — feel free to add anything technical.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: Long-context evals and next steps — technical notes

Hey Jared — quick technical answers to your questions and a proposed short-run we can do once you share samples.

1) Native context support:
- Redwood-13B-32k: native window up to ~32k tokens. Beyond that, the model will truncate by default.
- Redwood-RT-30B: tuned for longer-context coherence and supports offload/extended windows via segmented attention; practical upper bound depends on latency targets and hardware but we routinely run extended-eval scenarios with NVMe-backed KV cache.

2) Truncation behavior + chunking:
- Truncation is model dependent; when you exceed native window we recommend chunk+RAG/stitching. For summarization fidelity on very long docs, stitching (chunk-level summaries then meta-summary) preserves more global context than naive truncation.

3) Latency/cost ballpark (very rough):
- Redwood-13B-32k (quantized): p95 token-latency ~80–150ms depending on batch; estimated baseline cost for a steady 100 qps workload ~ $Xk/month (we'll provide exact sizing after we see sample distribution).
- Redwood-RT-30B: higher cost, lower error rate on summaries for very long contexts. Expect ~1.5–2x cost relative to 13B for same throughput.

4) Data residency:
- We can run the eval in US-only infra and provide an SOC2-compatible audit trail. We'll include the region in the eval config and produce logs for procurement.

Proposed small-run: you share one redacted 50k doc + 3 reference summaries. We'll run 3 models (13B-32k, RT-30B, 7B-8k baseline with chunking) and return the CSV with per-sample outputs, failure-mode notes, and a short recommendations section. We can turn this around in ~48hrs after we have the sample and access.

If you're ok, I'll provision a small eval job and send a short-run results link.

— Ben
